questions.question_text: Find the coordinates of the point on the curve $y = x^2 - 3x + 4$ where the tangent has gradient $5$.

options.why: Found $x = 4$ correctly but wrote the given gradient $5$ as the $y$-coordinate instead of substituting $x = 4$ into $y = x^2 - 3x + 4$.
Sign slip in the derivative: solved $2x + 3 = 5$ instead of $2x - 3 = 5$, giving $x = 1$, then evaluated $y = 1 - 3 + 4 = 2$.
Made both slips: solved $2x + 3 = 5$ to get $x = 1$, then reported the gradient $5$ as the $y$-coordinate instead of evaluating the curve.

questions.question_text:
The normal to the curve $y = 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 11x + 4$ at point $P(x, y)$ with $x > 0$ is perpendicular to $x - y + 3 = 0$.
Find the coordinates of $P$.

options.why: Ignored the domain restriction x greater than zero and gave the negative solution.
Used the target tangent gradient as the y-coordinate instead of substituting into the curve.
Substituted x into the derivative rather than the original cubic curve equation.

questions.solution_text:
$x - y + 3 = 0 \implies y = x + 3$ with gradient $1$.
Since the normal is perpendicular to this line, $m_{\perp} = -1$.
Therefore, the tangent gradient is $m = -\dfrac{1}{-1} = 1$.
$f'(x) = 6x^2 - 6x - 11$
$6x^2 - 6x - 11 = 1$
$6x^2 - 6x - 12 = 0$
$6(x^2 - x - 2) = 0$
$6(x - 2)(x + 1) = 0$
$x = 2 \text{ or } x = -1$
Since $x > 0$, $x = 2$.
$y = 2(2)^3 - 3(2)^2 - 11(2) + 4 = 16 - 12 - 22 + 4 = -14$
The point is $(2, -14)$.
